description:
This schematic map illustrates various land cover and habitat types typically found within and adjacent to a coastal lagoon ecosystem. The map uses distinct colours to represent different features, corresponding to a classification system.

The legend defines the following colour-coded features:
*   Light blue: Lagoon (labelled with code 8.3.1)
*   Yellow: Sand bank, and Beaches and Dunes (labelled with code 6.2.1)
*   Grey: Reed beds and marsh plants, encompassing Salt marshes (labelled with code 7.2.1) and Natural & semi-natural water courses (labelled with code 8.1.1)
*   Light blue lines within grey areas: Rivers
*   Dark blue: Sea and ocean, including Coastal waters (labelled with code 8.4.2)
*   Light green: Irrigated land, and Arable irrigated and non-irrigated land (labelled with code 2.1.1)
*   Dark olive green: Sclerophyllous scrub (labelled with code 5.3)

The spatial pattern shows a large central Lagoon (8.3.1) connected to the Sea and ocean (8.4.2 Coastal waters) via an opening in a long, yellow Sand bank (6.2.1 Beaches and Dunes). A river system (light blue lines within 8.1.1 Natural & semi-natural water courses) flows into the lagoon area, surrounded by grey areas of Salt marshes (7.2.1) and Reed beds and marsh plants. Inland, the landscape transitions to areas of Sclerophyllous scrub (5.3) and Arable irrigated and non-irrigated land (2.1.1). A smaller section of Beaches and Dunes (6.2.1) is also visible along the coast. No scale bar, compass, or specific geographic location is provided, indicating this is a conceptual diagram.
